result.reason: The redline adds contractor use and permits transfer in specified successor transactions, but it does not provide that paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable or that subscription licences may be terminated only for uncured material breach. It also unnecessarily grants Garman the same consent-free assignment right, altering Sparkling's protection against vendor assignment. The drafting is generally workable, but the licence remains facially “non-transferable” without an express exception in the grant itself, creating avoidable tension with Section 20(d).
